title: Legora acquires legal AI startup Wexler in fifth acquisition in 2026
excerpt: Legora has acquired London startup Wexler to better serve trial lawyers. The deal continues an acquisition spree for the Swedish-born software maker.
content_html:
Artificial intelligence has gotten much better at drafting legal documents. Now one legal-tech giant wants to make sure the facts behind them are right.

Legora has acquired the litigation startup Wexler, whose software helps lawyers reconstruct cases from thousands of documents. Lawyers can then trace something a witness or another attorney says back to the source and spot where it conflicts with the evidence. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The acquisition is a bid to make Legora more useful to trial lawyers. Much of its software has focused on helping lawyers research, review, and draft documents. Wexler brings it closer to the courtroom.

Disputes turn on the facts of a case, and how the law applies to them, Wexler cofounder and chief executive Gregory Mostyn said. Lawyers can spend weeks combing through thousands of documents to find those facts and sort them into a timeline. Wexler says its software cuts that manual review time by 75%.

The acquisition is Legora's fifth since January. Legora and its larger rival, Harvey, have spent the year buying smaller startups as they race to mop up the law firm market. The deals let them add new products and experienced teams faster than they could build them from scratch.

Mostyn says Wexler wasn't for sale.

The London-based startup had raised $7 million to expand beyond its British roots, and its software was being used by global law firms like HSF Kramer, Goodwin Procter, and Clifford Chance. Mostyn said he was fielding offers for a Series A when Legora came knocking.

He and his cofounder, Kush Madlani, flew to Stockholm to meet the Legora team. A smoked fish dinner with Legora executive Max Junestrand helped settle the question. The chance to bring Wexler's technology to a platform with more than 1,500 customers was too good to pass up, Mostyn said.

The legal tech boom is giving way to a shakeout. Law firms have tested a surge of chatbots and other software in the past few years and are now choosing which software companies to sign up with for the long term. The startups that build for one-off use cases may need buyers with deeper pockets and broader distribution.

Legora and Harvey are driving that consolidation. Both have raised hundreds of millions of dollars in their battle to become the default app for legal work. Legora was valued at $5.5 billion in March. Harvey is worth $11 billion.

Mostyn said Wexler's decision to focus on one complex part of litigation, rather than build a broad legal chatbot, has paid off. He described its software as a "scalpel, not a Swiss Army knife."

With the acquisition, Legora is betting that Wexler's scalpel can give its broader platform a sharper edge.

content_html_zh:
人工智能在起草法律文件方面已经做得更好了。 现在，一家法律科技巨头希望确保其背后的事实是正确的。

Legora 收购了诉讼初创公司 Wexler，该公司的软件可以帮助律师从数千份文档中重建案件。 然后，律师可以追溯到证人或另一位律师所说的内容，并找出其与证据相冲突的地方。 交易条款并未披露。

此次收购旨在让 Legora 对审判律师更有用。 其大部分软件都专注于帮助律师研究、审查和起草文件。 韦克斯勒让它更接近法庭。

Wexler 联合创始人兼首席执行官格雷戈里·莫斯廷 (Gregory Mostyn) 表示，争议取决于案件事实以及法律如何适用于案件。 律师可以花费数周时间梳理数千份文件，以找到这些事实并将其整理到时间表中。 Wexler 表示，其软件将人工审核时间缩短了 75%。

此次收购是 Legora 自 1 月份以来的第五次收购。 Legora 及其规模​​更大的竞争对手 Harvey 这一年一直在收购规模较小的初创公司，以竞相占领律师事务所市场。 这些交易使他们能够比从头开始构建新产品和经验丰富的团队更快地添加新产品和经验丰富的团队。

莫斯廷说韦克斯勒是非卖品。

这家总部位于伦敦的初创公司已筹集 700 万美元，用于拓展其英国本土业务，其软件被 HSF Kramer、Goodwin Procter 和 Clifford Chance 等全球律师事务所使用。 莫斯廷表示，当莱戈拉来敲门时，他正在接受 A 轮融资。

他和联合创始人 Kush Madlani 飞往斯德哥尔摩与 Legora 团队会面。 与 Legora 高管 Max Junestrand 共进的熏鱼晚餐帮助解决了这个问题。 Mostyn 表示，将 Wexler 的技术引入拥有 1,500 多个客户的平台的机会实在是太好了，不容错过。

合法技术的繁荣正在让位于一场洗牌。 律师事务所在过去几年中测试了大量的聊天机器人和其他软件，现在正在选择与哪些软件公司进行长期签约。 为一次性用例而建立的初创公司可能需要财力雄厚、分布更广泛的买家。

Legora 和 Harvey 正在推动这一整合。 两家公司都筹集了数亿美元，力争成为法律工作的默认应用程序。 Legora 3 月份的估值为 55 亿美元。 哈维身价110亿美元。

莫斯廷表示，韦克斯勒决定专注于诉讼的一个复杂部分，而不是建立一个广泛的法律聊天机器人，这一决定已经得到了回报。 他将其软件描述为“手术刀，而不是瑞士军刀”。

通过此次收购，Legora 相信 Wexler 的手术刀可以为其更广泛的平台带来更锋利的优势。
